decisions.decision: The board agreed, individually, that it will not take an official position on the citizen petition to expand the water district, leaving the decision to the voters at the district meeting.
Article 4B (a candidate speaking opportunity) was deferred because one of the two candidates, Mr. Emkey, could not attend; the other candidate's invitation was withdrawn/deferred for equal treatment.

If the district vote passes, the board will also bring forward a boundary cleanup amendment to align the existing district line with the new proposed district boundary along the affected property lines.
The superintendent plans to call a special district meeting in May to seek authorization to borrow for the SRF-funded project, with a possible second attempt in June if the first vote fails.
Residents with questions should call the water district or ask to be placed on a meeting agenda; the district will not respond to questions or accusations posted on social media.
Public comment going forward will be limited to about three minutes per speaker and kept as one-way comment rather than a back-and-forth with commissioners.

minutes.headline: Board defended SRF/PFAS funding against a resident group's bid to block it; a 29-year commissioner's last meeting
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District heard a developer's petition to expand the district for a 17-lot Birch Street subdivision, headed to a vote at Saturday's special district meeting, and discussed hiring Tighe & Bond to pursue a state grant for a Lancaster Shirley Road water main extension. Much of the meeting centered on a dispute with a resident group, described as opposing SRF/PFAS treatment-plant funding, which had lobbied MassDEP to pull the district's funding; the superintendent defended the funding and warned of much higher bond-financing costs if it is lost, and outlined plans for a May special meeting to seek borrowing authorization. The meeting closed with tributes to and a lengthy, contentious farewell from Commissioner John Esposito, who is retiring after 29 years.

what_happened.line: The board defended state SRF/PFAS funding for the treatment plant against a resident group's effort to have MassDEP withdraw it, warning that bond financing instead would cost far more.
A developer's petition to expand the water district for a 17-lot Birch Street subdivision heads to a vote at Saturday's special district meeting; the board took no official position.
The superintendent plans to call a special district meeting in May to seek voter authorization to borrow for the SRF-funded project, with a possible second try in June.
The board adopted a new rule limiting public comment to about three minutes per speaker, one-way, and said it will not respond to questions or accusations raised on social media.
The meeting closed with tributes and a lengthy, contentious farewell from Commissioner John Esposito, retiring after 29 years, including his rebuttal to residents' criticisms.

why_it_matters: Residents will be asked to vote on expanding the water district Saturday, and separately on borrowing authorization for the treatment plant at a special meeting expected in May or June.

How the treatment-plant project is financed -- state SRF funding versus municipal bonds -- affects what water rates end up covering, since the board says bond financing would add a transfer well above the SRF cost.
The new three-minute, one-way public comment format and the board's refusal to answer social-media questions change how residents can raise concerns with the board going forward.
